1. Lighthouses are typically painted with high-contrast color patterns, such as black and white stripes or red and white bands, to make them recognizable during the day.
2. The Fresnel lens, invented in the early 19th century, was a major technological advancement that allowed lighthouse beams to be seen from much greater distances.
3. Many historic lighthouses are now automated and no longer require resident keepers, though some still maintain a tradition of guided tours.
